topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture on cancer therapy and outlines its main learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address standard treatment modalities, including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside non-specific drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore targeted therapeutic strategies that take advantage of specific cell cycle defects, hormone dependencies, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine oncogene addiction, small-molecule kinase inhibitor design, and the diverse evolutionary pathways leading to inhibitor resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms and clinical utility of engineered monoclonal antibodies and targeted antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-based treatments
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate natural tumor immune surveillance and explore therapeutic strategies that harness, unblock, or genetically engineer T cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the systemic obstacles in cancer treatment, the impact of prevention and combination therapy on mortality, and future therapeutic paradigms.
